debrief.text:
Analyst
-------
  [warning] Blue got the spike down but could not hold it -- only 25% of its plants converted into round wins.
           rule: analyst.post_plant_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Red got the spike down but could not hold it -- only 40% of its plants converted into round wins.
           rule: analyst.post_plant_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue was out-traded across the match, taking 45% of round kills over 20 rounds against a 50% even split (sim-approx: kill share stands in for real trade windows).
           rule: analyst.trade_efficiency, 20 feature row(s) cited
  [info] R10 was the match's pivotal round -- the largest single swing (0.202) in the win-probability proxy. Red took it, Blue lost it.
           rule: analyst.pivotal_round, 4 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Red reached a plant in only 42% of its attack rounds -- most of those rounds were lost before the spike ever went down.
           rule: analyst.plant_rate, 1 feature row(s) cited

Economist
---------
  [warning] Blue force-bought 3 rounds back to back (R1, R2, R3). One force is a read; a run this long means the team never got off the back foot long enough to rebuild.
           rule: economist.consecutive_force, 3 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Red force-bought 3 rounds back to back (R1, R2, R3). One force is a read; a run this long means the team never got off the back foot long enough to rebuild.
           rule: economist.consecutive_force, 3 feature row(s) cited
  [warning] Blue force-bought in 8 of 20 rounds (40%), past the 30% mark where forcing stops being a read and starts being a habit.
           rule: economist.force_buy_frequency, 20 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Blue stole 0 of its 1 eco rounds (0%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited
  [info] Red stole 1 of its 1 eco rounds (100%).
           rule: economist.eco_conversion, 2 feature row(s) cited

provenance.detail: val-match-v1 requires a Riot production key. Matches here are generated by an in-repo simulator that emits payloads in the documented val-match-v1 shape, grounded in real agent and map UUIDs fetched live from val-content-v1. Nothing is scraped and no unofficial API is used. Every module downstream of the match adapter is source-agnostic, so live data swaps in with no code change.
provenance.note: Simulated data conforming to the val-match-v1 schema — production key application pending
